prompts.title: Azure Well-Architected review
prompts.description: Get a structured review of an Azure architecture against the five Well-Architected pillars, with prioritized fixes.

prompts.title: Bicep module generator
prompts.description: Generate a clean, parameterized and secure-by-default Bicep module for any Azure resource.
prompts.body:
Act as an Azure infrastructure-as-code expert. Write a production-ready Bicep module that deploys {{Azure resource}}.

Requirements:
- Target API version: the latest stable one you know of. Say which one you used.
- Parameters with @description, sensible defaults and @allowed values where relevant.
- Secure by default: private networking when the service supports it, TLS 1.2 minimum, managed identity, public network access disabled, diagnostic settings sent to a Log Analytics workspace passed as a parameter.
- Naming follows this convention: {{Naming convention}}
- Tags passed as an object parameter.
- Outputs: resource ID, name and any endpoint a consumer would need.

Follow the Azure Verified Modules (AVM) style. After the code, give a short example of how to call the module from a main.bicep file, and list the security choices you made.

prompts.title: Improve my prompt
prompts.description: A meta-prompt that rewrites your prompt to be clearer, more specific and more reliable.
prompts.body:
You are a prompt engineering expert. Improve the prompt below so that an LLM gives a more accurate, useful and consistent answer.

My prompt:
"""
{{Your prompt}}
"""

Goal of the prompt: {{What you want to get}}

Steps:
1. Diagnose the prompt in a few bullets: ambiguity, missing context, missing output format, missing constraints.
2. Ask me up to 3 questions only if they would change the result a lot.
3. Write the improved prompt. Include a role, context, the task, constraints, the expected output format and an example if useful. Mark anything I must fill in as a placeholder wrapped in double curly braces.
4. Explain in 3 bullets what you changed and why.

prompts.title: KQL query builder
prompts.description: Turn a plain-language question into a commented KQL query for Log Analytics, Microsoft Sentinel or Azure Resource Graph.
variables: Target (Log Analytics, Sentinel or Resource Graph)
prompts.body:
You are a Kusto Query Language (KQL) expert. Write a query for {{Target (Log Analytics, Sentinel or Resource Graph)}} that answers this question:

"{{Your question}}"

Known tables or columns (optional): {{Tables or columns}}

Requirements:
- Filter on time early (default: the last 24 hours) and project only the useful columns.
- Comment each step with //.
- Prefer summarize and render for anything that is a trend.
- If a table name is a guess, say so and suggest how to check it.

After the query, explain in three bullet points how it works and one way to turn it into an alert rule.

prompts.title: Azure cost optimization plan
prompts.description: Analyze an Azure cost export and get a prioritized FinOps action plan with estimated savings.
variables: Context (production or not, working hours, growth)
prompts.body:
Act as an Azure FinOps practitioner. Here is a summary of my monthly Azure spend (service, resource, SKU, cost, usage):

{{Cost data}}

Environment context: {{Context (production or not, working hours, growth)}}

Produce:
1. The top cost drivers and whether each looks normal.
2. Quick wins (rightsizing, shutting down idle resources, deleting orphaned disks and IPs, cheaper storage tiers).
3. Commitment options (Reservations, Savings Plan, Azure Hybrid Benefit) with the break-even reasoning.
4. Architecture changes worth considering for the long term.
5. A table of actions with estimated monthly savings, effort and risk.

State your assumptions clearly. Do not recommend anything that would reduce production reliability without flagging it.

prompts.title: Blameless incident postmortem
prompts.description: Turn raw incident notes into a clear, blameless postmortem with a timeline, root cause and follow-up actions.
prompts.body:
You are an experienced SRE. Write a blameless postmortem from the raw notes below.

Raw notes, chat logs and timestamps:
{{Incident notes}}

Use this structure:
1. Summary (3 sentences: what happened, impact, how it was fixed)
2. Impact (users, services, duration, SLA or SLO consumed)
3. Timeline in UTC as a table (time, event, source)
4. Root cause, using the "5 whys" method
5. What went well and what went wrong
6. Action items as a table (action, owner role, priority, type: prevent, detect or mitigate)

Stay factual and blameless: describe systems and processes, never people. Mark clearly any point you had to assume.

prompts.title: Convert Terraform to Bicep
prompts.description: Translate Terraform (azurerm) code into equivalent, idiomatic Bicep and flag what does not map one to one.
prompts.body:
Convert the following Terraform code that uses the azurerm provider into idiomatic Bicep.

```hcl
{{Terraform code}}
```

Rules:
- Map each azurerm resource to its Microsoft.* resource type and a stable API version.
- Turn variables into Bicep parameters (keep descriptions and defaults) and locals into variables.
- Use symbolic references instead of hard-coded resource IDs, and existing resources where Terraform used data sources.
- Replace count and for_each with Bicep loops.

Then add a section named "Not a 1:1 mapping" that lists anything that behaves differently (state, lifecycle blocks, provider-only features) and how to handle it.

prompts.title: GitHub Actions workflow
prompts.description: Generate a secure GitHub Actions workflow with OIDC to Azure, least-privilege permissions and caching.

prompts.title: LinkedIn post from an article
prompts.description: Turn a technical article or release note into an engaging, non-cringe LinkedIn post.
variables: Audience (for example, Azure architects, developers, IT managers)
prompts.body:
Write a LinkedIn post in {{Output language}} based on the content below.

{{Article text or link summary}}

Audience: {{Audience (for example, Azure architects, developers, IT managers)}}

Guidelines:
- First line: a hook under 15 words that makes people click "see more", with no clickbait.
- 3 to 5 short paragraphs or bullets with the key takeaways and why they matter in practice.
- One personal insight or opinion, written in the first person.
- End with an open question to invite comments.
- At most 3 hashtags and 2 emoji. No buzzwords like "game changer" or "revolutionize".
- Under 1,300 characters.

Then give 2 alternative hooks.

prompts.title: Meeting notes to action items
prompts.description: Turn a messy transcript or notes into a crisp summary, decisions and an owner-based action list.
prompts.body:
Here are the notes or the transcript of a meeting about {{Meeting topic}}:

{{Notes or transcript}}

Write, in {{Output language}}:
1. A 5-line executive summary.
2. The decisions made (one bullet each).
3. A table of action items: action, owner, due date (write "TBD" when unknown).
4. Open questions and risks.
5. A short follow-up email I can send to attendees.

Do not invent decisions or owners that are not in the notes.

prompts.title: Thorough code review
prompts.description: Ask for a senior-level code review focused on bugs, security and maintainability, not style nitpicks.
prompts.body:
Act as a senior {{Language}} engineer doing a code review. Review the code below.

```
{{Code to review}}
```

Focus on, in this order:
1. Bugs and logic errors (edge cases, null handling, concurrency, off-by-one errors).
2. Security issues (injection, secrets, authorization, unsafe deserialization).
3. Performance problems that matter at scale.
4. Maintainability: naming, duplication, overly complex functions.

Ignore pure formatting and style preferences. For each finding, give the line or snippet, why it is a problem, a severity and a suggested fix as code. If the code is good, say so briefly instead of inventing problems.
